source_state_policy: Catalog does not imply slide PDF, reading paper, or homework handout fulltext ingestion

lectures.title: Introduction — What Are Agentic Systems?
lectures.description: The spectrum from monolithic models to compound AI systems to agents; when compound systems win; the three engineering challenges (decomposition, data, evaluation); course logistics.

readings.text: Zaharia et al. "The Shift from Models to Compound AI Systems." BAIR Blog (2024).
Ng. "Agentic Design Patterns Part 1: Four AI Agent Strategies…" The Batch (2024).
Si et al. "Towards Execution-Grounded Automated AI Research." arXiv (2026).

lectures.title: LLMs for Builders
lectures.description: Language model internals for agent builders: decoding strategies, transformer attention (including linear and hybrid) and context length, the pretraining-to-post-training pipeline, inference and test-time scaling, structured I/O and constrained decoding, and context engineering.

lectures.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
lectures.description: Grounding and hallucination, embeddings and vector stores, chunking strategies, hybrid search, cross-encoders and late interaction (ColBERT). Hands-on: build a RAG pipeline from scratch.

readings.text: Schluntz & Zhang. "Building Effective Agents." Anthropic (2024).
Rajasekaran et al. "Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents." Anthropic (2025).
Lewis et al. "Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks." NeurIPS (2020).
Khattab & Zaharia. "ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Late Interaction over BERT." SIGIR (2020).

lectures.title: Tool Use & Function Calling
lectures.description: The REPL, function-calling APIs, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), designing good tools, code-execution sandboxes, error handling and retries. Hands-on: build a tool-using system from scratch.

lectures.title: Frameworks & Orchestration
lectures.description: DSPy (signatures, modules, optimizers), LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex; what frameworks abstract vs. what you built from scratch; choosing the right level of abstraction.

readings.text: Model Context Protocol Specification. The Linux Foundation (2025).
Khattab et al. "DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines." ICLR (2024).

lectures.title: Agent Design Patterns & Scaffolds
lectures.description: The workflows-vs-agents taxonomy, five composable workflow patterns, agent patterns (ReAct, plan-and-execute, reflection), and scaffolds as design decisions.

lectures.title: Agent Memory Architectures
lectures.description: Short- vs. long-term memory, memory as tool-based actions, the file system as externalized memory, structured memory paradigms, and cross-agent memory.

readings.text: Yao et al. "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models." ICLR (2023).
Packer et al. "MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems." arXiv (2023).
Letta. "Agent Memory: How to Build Agents that Learn and Remember." Letta Blog (2025).
Chhikara et al. "Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory." arXiv (2025).
Park et al. "Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior." UIST (2023).

lectures.title: Multi-Agent Systems
lectures.description: Single vs. multi-agent architectures, orchestration patterns, handoffs and state transfer, delegation and collaboration patterns, and the challenges of coordination and error propagation.

lectures.title: Optimization
lectures.description: The landscape from prompts to fine-tuning; prompt optimization (GEPA, MIPROv2, OPRO, TextGrad); test-time compute scaling; LoRA/QLoRA; distillation; RLHF/DPO at a high level; and when to optimize prompts vs. weights vs. inference compute.

readings.text: Wu et al. "AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation." COLM (2024).
Cemri et al. "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?" arXiv (2025).
Neubig. "Don't Sleep on Single-agent Systems." OpenHands Blog (2024).
Liu et al. "A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration." COLM (2024).
Snell et al. "Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally…" ICLR (2025).
Agrawal et al. "GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform RL." arXiv (2026).
Soylu et al. "Fine-Tuning and Prompt Optimization: Two Great Steps that Work Better Together." EMNLP (2024).
Opsahl-Ong et al. "Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs." arXiv (2024).

lectures.title: What Data Do Agents Need?
lectures.description: Traces, demonstrations, and feedback; data for optimization vs. evaluation; data flywheels; synthetic data generation; collecting data from human-agent interaction.

readings.text: Shankar. "Data Flywheels for LLM Applications." (2024).
Tan et al. "Large Language Models for Data Annotation and Synthesis: A Survey." EMNLP (2024).

lectures.title: Data Selection & Quality
lectures.description: Finding maximally informative data, filtering and selection strategies, tiny-but-targeted benchmarks, annotation practices, quality assessment, and building datasets from agent traces.

lectures.title: Evaluation Fundamentals & Benchmark Design
lectures.description: Why evals are hard, the 4-tuple framework (request, environment, stopping criteria, scorer), designing each component, properties of good benchmarks, realistic scaffolding, and reliability dimensions.

readings.text: Yang et al. "SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents." NeurIPS D&B (2025).
Shankar et al. "Who Validates the Validators? Aligning LLM-Assisted Evaluation with Human Preferences." UIST (2024).
Zhou et al. "LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment." NeurIPS (2023).
Zhu et al. "Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks." (2025).
Press. "How to Build Good Language Modeling Benchmarks." (2024).
Polo et al. "tinyBenchmarks: Evaluating LLMs with Fewer Examples." ICML (2024).

lectures.title: LLM-as-Judge & Evaluation Infrastructure
lectures.description: The three grader types, designing judge prompts, known biases, pairwise vs. pointwise evaluation, non-determinism metrics (pass@k vs. pass^k), harness design, and Anthropic's 8-step roadmap.

lectures.title: Agent Safety & Guardrails
lectures.description: Privacy risks of tool access, prompt injection (including indirect injection), red-teaming, sandboxing and permission models, output guardrails, liability considerations, responsible deployment, and human-in-the-loop patterns.

readings.text: Grace et al. "Demystifying Evals for AI Agents." Anthropic (2026).
Zheng et al. "Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena." NeurIPS (2023).
Ryan et al. "AutoMetrics: Approximate Human Judgements with Automatically Generated Evaluators." ICLR (2026).
Zhu et al. "AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Human Feedback." ICLR (2026).
Shao et al. "PrivacyLens: Evaluating Privacy Norm Awareness of LMs in Action." NeurIPS D&B (2024).
Zhang & Yang. "Searching for Privacy Risks in LLM Agents via Simulation." arXiv (2025).
Li. "Agentic LLMs as Powerful Deanonymizers." arXiv (2026).
Wen et al. "Contextualized Privacy Defense for LLM Agents." arXiv (2026).
OpenAI. "Understanding Prompt Injections: A Frontier Security Challenge." (2025).
Anthropic. "Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy." (2023).

lectures.title: Coding & Software Agents
lectures.description: How coding agents work end-to-end; SWE-agent, Claude Code, and OpenHands architectures; scaffolds as design decisions; SWE-bench and the 4-tuple framework in practice; the future of software development with agents.

readings.text: Yang et al. "SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering." NeurIPS (2024).
Wang et al. "OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers." ICLR (2025).
Anthropic. "Claude Code: Best Practices for Agentic Coding." (2025).
Young. "Effective Harnesses for Long-Running Agents." Anthropic (2025).
Jimenez et al. "SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?" ICLR (2024).

lectures.title: Proactive Agents
lectures.description: From reactive to proactive; General User Models (GUM); Next Action Prediction; open-source proactive personal agents; privacy and trust implications; and when agents should initiate vs. wait (mixed initiative).

lectures.title: Frontiers & Open Problems
lectures.description: Multimodal agents, web agents and computer use, science agents, long-running agent architectures, production and observability (tracing, monitoring, cost management), and open problems in reliability, scalability, and interpretability.

readings.text: Shaikh et al. "Creating General User Models from Computer Use." UIST (2025).
Shaikh et al. "Learning Next Action Predictors from Human-Computer Interaction." arXiv (2026).
Steinberger. "OpenClaw: Open-source proactive AI agent." (2025).
Xie et al. "OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real Computer Environments." NeurIPS D&B (2024).
Yao et al. "WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents." NeurIPS (2022).
